title.narrative: Strengthening Technical and Vocational Education and Training

description.narrative:
The impact of the proposed Strengthening Technical and Vocational Education and Training Project (the project) will be a national workforce with an increased proportion of skilled workers employed in Tajikistan. The outcome will be a demand-driven, quality-assured, and flexible TVET system responsive to labor market needs.
The project comprises four outputs, as follows: (i) TVET system methodology modernized; (ii) physical learning facilities in selected TVET institutions upgraded; (iii) access to quality TVET programs improved; and (iv) governance and management of TVET system strengthened. These are explained below.
Output 1: TVET system methodology modernized. The project will develop competency standards and assessment tools aligned to an adapted European Qualification Framework (EQF). Competency-based training (CBT) curriculum and gender-sensitive learning materials will be developed, and competency assessors for 17 occupations will be trained. The occupations have been selected based on the government's development priorities, a labor market survey conducted during project preparation, and inputs from key stakeholders. An implementation plan for the development of the CBT components has been developed involving industry sector working groups, training providers, and development partners. Guidelines and manuals will be prepared to promote future sustainability and institutionalize tasks related to development of competency standards, qualifications and curriculum. The Center for Training Methodology and Monitoring of Education Quality (CTMMEQ) under MOLME will take the lead in implementing Output 1. The project will build CTMMEQ capacity a twinning partnership with a reputable foreign workforce development agency. The CBT curriculum and learning materials will be piloted in 29 TVET institutions. The project will strengthen the selected TVET institutions' core programs to enable them to serve as resource centers for other TVET institutions in their respective sectors.
Output 2: Physical learning facilities in selected TVET institutions upgraded. The project will upgrade the physical learning and teaching facilities of the selected TVET institutions. The design of rehabilitation works takes into consideration teaching requirements, student needs, and environmental and social safeguards. In three project sites, green reconstruction and power approaches will demonstrate options for general building rehabilitation, and help train teachers and students in green reconstruction. The project will also support gender-appropriate dormitory upgrades, which will help increase female student access to formal TVET system.
Output 3: Access to quality TVET programs improved. The project will develop an in-service TVET teachers training plan to provide teachers and masters with a clear understanding of the CBT methodology, competencies n student-centered training delivery, and practical knowledge and skills in respective technology areas through industry internships.
Output 4: Governance and management strengthened. The project will support the establishment and operation of industry advisory committees and working groups in the five priority sectors; training in modern TVET management, strengthening of the secretariat of the National Coordination Council for Vocational Education and Training; provision of equipment for the Scientific Research Institute on Labour, Migration and Employment under MOLME to support annual labor market assessments; a social marketing program; development and implementation of the project monitoring and evaluation system; and designation of a resource center in each region to facilitate coordination and ensure efficient project implementation. A skills conference in year 4 will showcase CBT achievements.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: A demand-driven, quality-assured, and flexible TVET system responsive to labor market needs.

At least 50% (1,115) of the Gender Equity Model Program's beneficiaries received TVET certifications in non-traditional occupations (2015 baseline: 0) Achievement: 204.9 Progress/Status: As of March 2021, 2,482 beneficiaries had enrolled; out of which, 2,285 graduated and received certifications in non-traditional occupations.
The breakdown of number of beneficiaries who have received certifications by year are as follows: (i) Year 2018: 123, (ii) Year 2019: 950, (iii) Year 2020: 1,212.
1,542 have been employed. Data Source: MOLME tracer studies and annual reports

By 2022: Employer's satisfaction rate with quality of graduates in selected TVET institutions increased by 10% (sex-disaggregated baselines will be determined at the start of the tracer study) (2015 baseline: NA Achievement: 12 Progress/Status: The tracer study was completed in June 2021 with the draft report showing a 90% employer satisfaction rate, compared with the baseline rate of 78% as shown in the 2017 tracer study. Data Source: Employer satisfaction surveys

CBT assessment and certification system operation (2015 baseline: no system) Progress/Status: The 17 competency standards were approved by the MOLME Board on 26 November 2020.
The curricula for 17 occupations by facilitators and industry experts have been developed.
The CBT assessment and certification system have been developed and user training is ongoing.
As of March 2021, system training process is ongoing.
As of June 2021, all lyceums have access to the CBT assessment and certification system.
As of December 2021 the system has been piloted in project-targeted adult-learning centers and lyceums. 300 beneficiaries have been registered and reports on their usage were provided, according to which the system has been further improved. The formal adoption of the system goes beyond the project scope and in the final Inter-agency Steering Group (ISG) meeting held on 6 May 2022 further instructions have been given in this regard. Project prepared and submitted all the necessary documents (decrees and guidelines) to MOLME and the system is operational now. MOLME departments and devisions are instructed to further implement the system in TVET. Data Source: Project progress reports Base year: 2015 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: (1) TVET system methodology modernized Indicator: CBT curriculum and gender-sensitive learning materials for 17 occupations endorsed by industry expert panels and approved by MOLME by Q3 2021 (2015 baseline: no curriculum) Progress/Status: As of March 2021, the curriculum for 17 occupations by facilitators and industry experts has been completed and concurred by the Committee of Language and Terminology.
The authorized body to approve the curricula is the CTMMEQ, not the MOLME.
The curriculum for 17 occupations was approved by CTMMEQ on 9 July 2021 and will be disseminated (Tajik version) to project lyceums by November 2021. The Russian version was disseminated to project lyceums in October 2021. The e-content will also be provided in softcopies to lyceums, and uploaded in the MOLME website (the website is being updated by MOLME).
10 gender sensitive learning materials have been developed by industry experts and were endorsed by CTMMEQ on 9 July 2021. Dissemination of the Tajik version will be by end November 2021 (the Russian version has already been disseminated).
As of December 2021, all curricula and learning materials have been printed and delivered to project selected institutions. Data Source: MOLME approvals, project progress reports
Actual value:

Output: (1) TVET system methodology modernized Indicator: Occupational standards and assessment tools for 17 selected occupations endorsed by industry working groups and approved by MOLME by 2020 (2015 baseline: no standards) Progress/Status: The competency standards for 17 occupations were developed in December 2019, validated by industries, and translated into Tajik and approved by the Committee on Terminology and Language of Tajikistan.
The competency standards for 17 occupations were approved by the MOLME Board on 26 November 2020. Data Source: MOLME approvals, project progress reports

As of December 2020, a total of 132 classrooms have been rehabilitated. By June 2021, a total of 155 classrooms have been rehabilitated. Data Source: MOLME annual reports, project progress reports Actual value:

As of December 2020, a total of 76 workshops have been rehabilitated. By June 2021, a total of 83 workshops have been rehabilitated. Data Source: MOLME annual reports, project progress reports Actual value:

Output: (2) Physical learning environment upgraded Indicator: Equipment packages for 17 occupations provided in five skill areas by Q1 2021 (2015 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: By August 2021, equipment for 16 out of the 17 occupations have been delivered (equivalent to 94% of occupations). The acceptance committee issued acceptance certificates in September 2021 for the recent delivery.
The remaining equipment under the last ICB lot (for vegetable farming and food processing occupations) was delivered in March 2022. It was delayed due to COVID-19 related restrictions at the export border; with the change of the export custom.
Data Source: MOLME annual reports, project progress reports Actual value:

Data Source: MOLME annual reports, project progress reports Actual value:

12,215 beneficiaries have been employed.
Data Source: MOLME tracer studies Actual value:

Output: (3) Access to quality TVET programs improved Indicator: At least 17,000 workers, most of whom are returning migrants, are technically assessed, with qualified migrants receiving skills certification, by Q1 2021 (2015 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: By Q1 2021, 29,571 beneficiaries have completed training, out of which 12,285 are females. Output: (3) Access to quality TVET programs improved Indicator: At least 90% of EPCD staff trained in CBT methodology by 2020 (2015 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: About 90% of EPCD and CTMMEQ staff were trained on CBT - teaching-training program (Volumes 1-2-3-4-5).
The project teacher training specialist conducted the initial training of 40 teachers and masters in October 2017. The second batch of training was conducted in March 2018, followed by the 3rd training in October 2018. Training completed in June 2019. Data Source: MOLME teacher training reports Actual value:

Output: (3) Access to quality TVET programs improved Indicator: At least 90% of TVET teachers and masters in selected occupations in selected TVET institutions (females account for a minimum of 35% of teachers and 25% of masters) trained in CBT methodology by Q1 2021 (2015 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: The first two stages were completed in August 2020, with more than 90% trained in CBT methodology.
All three stages were completed in April 2021 -- first stage on introduction of CBT methodology, second stage on development of competency standards, and last stage on curriculum and learning materials. 100% trained in CBT. methodology.
By 10 April 2021, a total of 707 teachers (100%) from pilot TVET institutions have been involved in 159 СВТ trainings and workshops, of which 350 or 44.3% are women.
By 10 April 2021, a total of 83 masters (100%) from pilot TVET institutions have been involved in 159 СВТ trainings and workshops, of which 38 or 45% are women.
Data Source: Project progress reports

Output: (4) Governance and management of TVET system strengthened Indicator: At least 80% directors and at least one senior staff member (includes 80% female senior management staff) of TVET institutions trained in modern educational management approaches by Q3 2021 (2015 baseline: 0). Progress/Status: By August 2019, 122 have been trained by BDO Academy (a firm) on the first part of training (domestically provided), including directors (61, including 11 women); and senior staff member (61, including 40 women or 65.6%) from a total of 61 TVET institutions, equivalent to 100%.
Nanyang Polytechnic International provided online training in March 2021 as the second part (in lieu of the oversea training due to COVID19) for 21 directors (including 7 women) and 21 senior staff members (including 10 women, or 47.6%).
(exceeded target for absolute numbers but not achieving the gender target for senior management staff) Data Source: MOLME reports Actual value:

Output: (1) TVET system methodology modernized Indicator: Competency assessment and certification system applied on a pilot basis to graduates in selected occupations by Q2 2021 (2015 baseline: no system) Progress/Status: As of March 2021, the system has been developed and installed. The targeted lyceums have been given access to the certification system. The system was piloted at an adult learning center from July 2021. The CBT expert's contract was extended from July to September 2021 to supervise and report on the pilot. The pilot was completed as of August 2021 for the selected training program (report was sent to ADB in November 2021). Wider use of the system in project-targeted adult learning centers and lyceums is ongoing for further feedback.
As of Dec 2021, the process of developing a mechanism for implementing the developed system into TVET is underway. Data Source: MOLME approvals, project progress reports

Progress/Status: As of March 2021, project-related informational and pro-materials have been disseminated to project's beneficiaries and stakeholders.
The social marketing firm has completed its task of developing and disseminating the documentaries on CBT and gender sensitivity mainstreaming; and conduct of all activities in 40 districts.
Data Source: MOLME tracer studies Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y

Data Source: MOLME reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y

Output: (4) Governance and management of TVET system strengthened Indicator: Industry advisory committees, with at least 20% female members, operational in selected TVET institutions by 2018 (2015 baseline: NA) Progress/Status: The industry advisory committees (IACs) were established in the 21 selected lyceums and 7 adult learning center branches, with 20% female, in September 2017.
The total number of IAC members is 230; out of this figure, 70 or 30.43% are women (teachers, masters, representatives of women's committees).
The IACs started operations upon its establishment in 2017, while the project provided equipment and furniture in 2018 to enhance their capacity. IACs received technical support (consultations, training, regulations, support of both international and local consultants, etc.) and equipment for working efficiently. Data Source: MOLME reports Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: not operational Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: not operational Target year: 2018 Target value: operational
